Briefing for 17 November 2026

Short items for 17 November 2026. Sapaude writes them in its own words. Where a longer article exists, the link goes there. The publisher is Sapaude.

AI agents

California sues OpenAI over rogue agent tests

California's attorney general says OpenAI tested dangerous models without proper safeguards and cites 80 incidents, including the Hugging Face hack. OpenAI disputes this, and no court has ruled yet.

Source: State of California DOJ

Device

US closes the remote route to AI chips for China

A new interim rule requires licenses for AI chips and servers sent to data centers anywhere in the world if they could provide compute to companies in China or other restricted countries.

Source: TechCrunch

Study · More technical

OpenAI lets outside testers inspect internal models

Apollo Research, METR, Transluce and Goodfire get deep access to checkpoints, code and monitoring to check alignment and safeguards. OpenAI says public reports from such reviews should show how labs handle risks.

Source: OpenAI

Everyday tool

Gemini keeps your chats without training on them

A new setting lets you keep your Gemini chat history while opting out of model training. With history off, new chats are still stored for about two months; the rollout starts in the coming weeks.

Source: Google

Everyday tool

Ask Maps comes to more than 30 European countries

Google's Gemini-based Ask Maps answers questions about places in plain language and can build trip itineraries with weather and parking info for each stop.

Source: Google

New model · More technical

Tencent's Hy4 flash cuts the price of everyday tasks

Hy4 flash has 224 billion parameters, only 12 billion of them active, takes multimodal input and handles up to 1 million tokens of context. Input costs about $0.07 per million tokens.

Source: Tencent

In the background

Hugging Face now routes open-weight models via OpenRouter

Inference Providers now send language model requests through OpenRouter, which picks a provider by price, speed and reliability. Your Hugging Face token and code stay the same.

Source: Hugging Face

In the background

EU drafts a template for AI Act rights checks

The Commission wants feedback on a questionnaire for deployers of high-risk AI systems who must assess fundamental rights impacts under Article 27. The duty applies from December 2027.

Source: European Commission

Be brave. Get smart.
